history.dynasty: unknown (rock-cut steps added by medieval Garhwal rulers)
history.summary: The famous cave temple of Koteshwar Mahadev, about 3 km from Rudraprayag town on the banks of the Alaknanda, at about 885 m altitude. The shrine sits inside a natural cave containing many naturally formed stalagmites worshipped as Shivalingas (the main linga is of dark stone), along with naturally formed idols of Parvati, Ganesha, Hanuman and Durga. Legend says Shiva stopped here to meditate on his way to Kedarnath and hid in this cave to escape the demon Bhasmasura. Medieval Garhwal rulers cut rock steps and pathways to reach the cave. The site is especially popular during Mahashivratri and Shravan; the cave is open year-round and reached by a staircase descent to the riverbank.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Rudraprayag is a holy town in the Garhwal Himalayas at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers. It is a key pilgrimage stop on the Char Dham route and the gateway to Kedarnath, combining river confluences, ancient temples and mountain scenery.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, about 160 km
travel.road: About 3 km from Rudraprayag town on the Rudraprayag-Guptkashi road; accessible by taxi and auto from the bus station, then a staircase descent to the cave

visitor_information.best_time: October to June; Mahashivratri and Shravan are the busiest times
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 7:00 PM daily (one source says 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM - hours conflict, verify locally); open all year, no entry fee
